meta.title: Support
meta.description: Get help with Bookmark Scout: answers to common problems, how to report a bug, and where to email about support, privacy, and security.

supportPage.title: Support
supportPage.intro: Most answers are in the docs and the FAQ. For anything else, email us. If something is broken, you can also report it in public on GitHub.

docs.title: Read the docs
docs.body: Installation for each browser, feature guides, and every setting explained.

faq.title: Check the FAQ
faq.body: Short answers about where your data goes, whether you need AI, and what works in Firefox.

firefoxRestart.q: Bookmark Scout disappears when I restart Firefox
a: The Firefox version is coming soon to Firefox Add-ons. Until then, Bookmark Scout installed by hand runs in Firefox as a temporary add-on, and Firefox removes temporary add-ons when it restarts.
Load it again after a restart: open about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox, click Load Temporary Add-on, and select the manifest.json file in the extracted folder.

firefoxManager.q: I can't find the bookmarks manager in Firefox
a: Firefox does not let extensions replace its bookmarks page, so the Bookmark Scout manager does not open from Firefox's own bookmarks menu.
Click Open bookmark manager (the books icon) at the top of the toolbar popup. The manager opens in a new tab, with the Tools sidebar, saved searches, and import and export.

firefoxIcons.q: Site icons are missing in Firefox
a: Bookmark Scout shows the browser's own cached icons, which Chrome and Edge share with extensions and Firefox does not. Sites you have not visited recently can show a generic globe in Chrome and Edge for the same reason.
Run Refresh Site Icons in the manager's Tools sidebar to download each site's own icon. Saved icons stay on this device. In Firefox, open the manager with Open bookmark manager in the toolbar popup.

quickSave.q: The quick save shortcut does nothing
a: If another extension already uses {{SHORTCUT:commands.quick-save}} or {{SHORTCUT:commands.ai-quick-save}}, the browser leaves Bookmark Scout's shortcut without keys, and the popup shows Quick save shortcut not set. Click Set it up, or open Settings, then Saving & Search, then Keyboard shortcuts, and choose other keys.
Some pages, such as the browser's own pages and the extension store, do not let extensions show anything on them. There the toolbar icon shows whether the page was saved, and the popup offers Undo.

dataReset.q: My settings are gone after an update
a: One update moved Bookmark Scout's saved data to a new format and removed the old data instead of converting it. Settings are back to their defaults, AI services and API keys need to be added again, and custom prompts, saved searches, tags, summaries, and saved site icons are gone. Your bookmarks are not touched.
If you saved your settings with Back up settings at the bottom of Settings before updating, use Restore settings there to bring them back.

websiteAccess.q: Check Dead Links, Metadata Fetcher, or Refresh Site Icons did not scan anything
a: These tools need access to websites, which Bookmark Scout does not get at install. The browser asks the first time you run them, and if you decline, nothing is scanned.
Run the tool again and allow access when the browser asks.

aiSetup.q: AI features are missing or do not respond
a: AI is optional and off by default. To use it, turn it on in Settings under AI, choose your AI company, and paste the key from your account there; the AI guide in the docs shows where to find it. A free AI program on your own computer, such as Ollama, needs no key.
Click Verify Service to test the connection. The first time, the browser asks for access to that provider's site; allow it so the extension can reach the provider.

report-a-bug.title: Report a bug
report-a-bug.body: Email the details to {supportEmail}. If you have a GitHub account, you can instead open a public issue, where anyone can follow the fix; search the existing issues first, in case someone has already reported it.

include.browser: Your browser and its version (Chrome, Edge, or Firefox).
include.version: The Bookmark Scout version, shown on your browser's extensions page.
include.steps: The steps that lead to the problem, starting from where you opened Bookmark Scout: the popup, side panel, or manager.
include.result: What you expected and what happened instead, including any error message.
include.screenshot: A screenshot if it helps, with private bookmarks hidden.

report-a-bug.privacyNote: GitHub issues are public. Never paste an API key, and leave out bookmark titles or URLs you do not want others to see.

support.title: Help with the extension
support.body: Questions about installing or using Bookmark Scout that you would rather not post in public.

privacy.title: Privacy questions and requests
privacy.body: Questions about how your data is handled. The <privacyPolicy>privacy policy</privacyPolicy> explains what the extension and the websites do with data.

security.title: Security vulnerabilities
security.body: Report vulnerabilities here privately, not in a public issue. See <securityPolicy>SECURITY.md</securityPolicy> and <securityTxt>security.txt</securityTxt>.
